nodes.content: Investigate causal effect identifiability reasoning from diagrams, distinguishing structural edits from equivalent redrawings across unseen graph compositions.
requirements: Achieve 85% paired accuracy on identifiability judgments before and after structural edits, including latent confounding.
Maintain 95% prediction consistency across equivalent redrawings of held-out graph compositions.

nodes.content: Train a diagram-to-ADMG encoder using ID-algorithm labels, structural-edit contrastive pairs, and redraw-invariance regularization on held-out graph compositions.
Can the diagram-to-ADMG encoder distinguish added latent confounding from visually rerouted, structurally unchanged edges in held-out graph compositions?
Contrastive ADMG training will achieve ≥85% paired accuracy for latent-confounder edits and ≥95% redraw consistency on unseen compositions.
Generate held-out ADMG compositions with confounder edits and equivalent redraws; train the encoder, then measure paired accuracy and redraw consistency.
Train the encoder on 12,000 ID-labeled ADMG diagrams; measure confounder-edit paired accuracy and redraw consistency across 2,000 held-out compositions.
On 2,000 held-out ADMG compositions, confounder-edit paired accuracy reached 87% and equivalent-redraw prediction consistency reached 96%.
Retain contrastive ADMG training for broader edit tests; confounder-edit accuracy and redraw consistency exceed their respective thresholds.
ADMG-Contrast v1 checkpoint and held-out evaluation report with ID-label predictions, 87% confounder-edit paired accuracy, and 96% redraw consistency.
Using ADMG-Contrast v1, score 1,000 unseen compositions before and after confounder removal and across equivalent redraws; recompute both metrics.
On 1,000 new compositions, confounder-removal paired accuracy was 79%, below the 85% threshold; redraw consistency remained 96%.
Bidirectional confounder-edit augmentation will raise held-out removal paired accuracy above 85% while preserving ≥95% redraw consistency.
Fine-tune ADMG-Contrast v1 on 4,000 new bidirectional confounder-edit pairs; measure removal paired accuracy and redraw consistency on 1,000 held-out compositions.
After bidirectional fine-tuning, confounder-removal paired accuracy rose from 79% to 86% on 1,000 held-out compositions; redraw consistency stayed 96%.
Build a symbolic edge parser that canonicalizes labeled ADMGs and applies the ID algorithm to each structural-edit pair.
Will canonical ADMG parsing preserve directed versus bidirected edges when held-out diagrams mix crossings, rerouting, and latent confounding?
Benchmark canonical edge parsing on crossed-edge redraws and bidirected-edge edits; compare parsed ADMGs and ID judgments against oracle graphs.
Using ADMG-Contrast v1, compare encoder versus canonical-parser ID judgments on 800 held-out confounder-edit/crossing-redraw pairs for paired accuracy and consistency.
Across 800 crossing-redraw/confounder-edit pairs, canonical parser versus ADMG-Contrast v1 achieved 90% versus 77% paired accuracy; 97% versus 89% redraw consistency.
Audit canonical-parser errors from the 800-pair comparison against oracle ADMGs, classifying crossing and bidirected-edge mismatches.
ParserAudit-800 catalogs oracle versus parsed edges for all 800 pairs, with crossing and bidirected-edge error tags.
Blindly reannotate 160 stratified ParserAudit-800 cases against oracle ADMGs; quantify crossing and bidirected-edge tag precision and recall.
On 160 reannotated ParserAudit-800 cases, crossing-tag precision/recall was 94%/91%; bidirected-edge-tag precision/recall was 89%/85%.
Prioritize canonical parsing for crossings, but cross-check confounder edits with the fine-tuned encoder given 85% bidirected-tag recall.
Fuse canonical ADMG parsing with the fine-tuned encoder, resolving ambiguous bidirected edges by comparing predictions across equivalent redraws.
Redraw-consensus fusion will achieve ≥90% paired accuracy across mixed confounder edits and ≥97% consistency on unseen redraws.
Does redraw-consensus fusion recover bidirected edges missed by canonical parsing without merging genuinely different confounder edits?
Fuse fine-tuned ADMG-Contrast v1 with canonical parsing; measure bidirected recall, edit-pair accuracy, and redraw consistency on 1,200 compositions.
On 1,200 compositions, fusion reached 88% mixed-edit paired accuracy, below the hypothesized 90%; redraw consistency reached 98%.
Audit fusion disagreements by bidirected-edge status, then tune consensus gating and retest edit preservation and redraw consistency.
Audit fusion disagreements; tune gates using ADMG-Contrast v1, then test 1,200 new compositions for paired accuracy and redraw consistency.
On 1,200 new compositions, gated fusion achieved 91% mixed-edit paired accuracy and 97% redraw consistency, meeting both hypothesis thresholds.
Does gated fusion retain paired accuracy on larger, multiply confounded ADMGs absent from the 1,200-composition evaluation?
On unseen 8–12-node ADMGs with multiple bidirected edges, gated fusion maintains ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% redraw consistency.
Power a held-out 8–12-node multiply-confounded ADMG test from ungated 88%/98% and gated 91%/97% findings; measure paired accuracy and redraw consistency.
On 600 unseen 8–12-node multiply-confounded ADMGs, gated fusion achieved 87% paired-edit accuracy and 96% redraw consistency.
Stratify ungated, gated, and 8–12-node fusion errors by bidirected-edge count; inspect structural edits incorrectly merged as redraws.
FusionErrorAtlas v1 catalogs errors across three evaluation cohorts by bidirected-edge count, including structural edits misclassified as redraws.
Use FusionErrorAtlas v1 to train an edge-change verifier separating latent-confounder edits from redraws before gated ID inference.
Can an edge-change verifier detect bidirected-edge additions masked by redraws without flagging harmless reroutings on multiply-confounded ADMGs?
Create matched confounder-addition/redraw pairs from FusionErrorAtlas v1; train an edge-change verifier and compare gated ID inference against unchanged fusion.
Train an edge-change verifier on FusionErrorAtlas v1; compare verifier-gated ID inference against unchanged fusion on 600 new confounder-addition/redraw pairs.
On 600 new pairs, verifier-gated versus unchanged fusion achieved 82% versus 87% paired accuracy and 94% versus 96% redraw consistency.
Which verifier errors cause harmless reroutings to trigger ID changes, degrading both paired accuracy and redraw consistency?
False-positive edge-change flags on crossed reroutings drive both failures; suppressing them restores ≥85% paired accuracy and ≥95% redraw consistency.
Using FusionErrorAtlas v1, audit crossed-rerouting false positives, calibrate verifier gates, and retest paired accuracy and redraw consistency on 600 pairs.
On 600 pairs, crossed-rerouting false positives fell 18%→7%; calibrated verifier achieved 89% paired accuracy and 96% redraw consistency.
Using FusionErrorAtlas v1 and both gating baselines, test multiply-confounded pairs for edit recall, redraw false alarms, and ID accuracy.
On 500 multiply-confounded pairs, calibrated gating achieved 91% edit recall, 6% redraw false alarms, and 88% paired accuracy.
EdgeVerify-Bench v1 provides 500 multiply-confounded edit/redraw pairs, oracle ADMGs, and verifier-gated ID predictions for reproducible auditing.
Use ID-sensitivity tests to target ambiguous bidirected edges for additional redraws, then aggregate parsed ADMGs before judging structural edits.
Can ID-sensitivity-guided redraws resolve uncertain bidirected edges without smoothing away genuine changes in identifiability?
Rank uncertain edges by ID-label sensitivity, generate three targeted redraws per diagram, and compare edit preservation with untargeted sampling.
Using ParserAudit-800 edge tags and EdgeVerify-Bench v1, compare three ID-sensitivity-targeted versus random redraws for paired accuracy and consistency.
On EdgeVerify-Bench v1, targeted versus random redraws achieved 90% versus 86% paired accuracy and 97% versus 95% consistency.
Use FusionErrorAtlas v1 mismerged-edit tags to select held-out pairs; quantify ID-label flips masked by validated targeted-redraw aggregation.
IDFlipAudit v1 lists held-out structural-edit pairs, oracle ID-label flips, and whether targeted-redraw aggregation masked each flip.
Using validated edge tags and initial-versus-calibrated gate benchmarks, audit IDFlipAudit v1 for masked ID flips and redraw consistency.
In IDFlipAudit v1, targeted aggregation masked 8/200 oracle ID flips (4%); equivalent-redraw consistency was 97% across 600 views.
Adopt calibrated verifier gating and targeted redraws, but abstain on uncertain edge changes because aggregation masked 4% of ID flips.
IDFlipAudit v1 validation report records 8/200 masked ID flips, 97% consistency across 600 redraws, and uncertain-edge abstention flags.
